newsitem.title: CHINA: China seen making 30 mln T wood-pulp paper in 2000.
newsitem.headline: China seen making 30 mln T wood-pulp paper in 2000.

text.p: China will make 30 million tonnes of wood-pulp paper a year by the end of the century, as domestic producers move to ease the nation's reliance on imports, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Chinese paper-makers were seeking foreign investment to help boost output, the agency said in a report late on Monday,
China now has 5,600 pulp and paper factories which produce 21.4 million tonnes of paper a year, state media has said.

"It is expected that China will boost its output of wood-pulp paper to 30 million tonnes by the year 2000, and the figure can reach 40 million by the year 2010," Xinhua quoted Vice-Minister of Forestry, Li Yucai, as saying.

China is ranked third in the world in terms of annual output of paper products, but Chinese per capita consumption of paper products was just 21 kg a year, less than half the world average, Xinhua said.
Production of paper made from wood pulp had been listed by Beijing as a key area for economic development, it said.
